title: Toolchain Fundamentals
subtitle: Verify the tools that turn source text into running bytes.
summary: Install and verify gcc, g++, nasm, gdb and python, and see exactly what each stage of compilation does.
learning_objectives: Verify gcc, g++, nasm, gdb and python are available and explain what each does.
Distinguish preprocessing, compilation, assembly and linking using gcc flags.
Use objdump and nm to inspect a built binary and explain sections.
prerequisites: From a C Library Call to a System Call

blocks.title: Why this matters
blocks.markdown: You cannot debug what you cannot build. Every later module assumes you can go from `hello.c` → `a.exe` → `objdump` without guessing.

A C program does not jump directly to machine code. `gcc -E` shows preprocessor output (headers expanded, macros applied). `gcc -S` emits assembly text. `as` assembles to an object file (`.o` with machine bytes plus relocations). `ld` links objects and libraries into an executable with resolved addresses.

Run each flag once on the same `hello.c` — once you see the intermediate files, the pipeline stops being magic.

blocks.explanation: Run each version check. On Windows with UCRT64 via MSYS2, gcc should report 12+; with the older mingw32 bundled, 6.3 is enough for modules 00-03 but upgrade for 04+.

blocks.title: Windows note
blocks.markdown: Use UCRT64 (not mingw32) for C++ 17/20, newer GDB, and consistent POSIX shims. `pacman -S mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-gcc mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-gdb nasm python` keeps the whole curriculum working.

blocks.explanation: Minimal hosted C program. It links against the C library by default; use -nostdlib later in assembly modules to avoid it.
blocks.build_command: gcc -E hello.c -o hello.i && wc -l hello.i; gcc -S hello.c -o hello.s && head -20 hello.s; gcc -c hello.c -o hello.o && nm hello.o | head
blocks.expected_output: hello.i has ~800 lines after headers; hello.s shows mov, call, ret; hello.o has T main

blocks.title: Binutils — objdump and nm
blocks.purpose: Learn to inspect sections, symbols and disassembly of object files.

blocks.question: What does gcc -S do without linking?
options: Assembles to machine code object (.o) and stops.
blocks.explanation: -E stops after preprocessing, -S after compilation to assembly, -c after assembling to an object. Linking is the final ld step.

blocks.title: Trace the build
blocks.objective: Produce and inspect all intermediate artefacts of a single C file.
blocks.environment: Any OS with gcc, binutils (objdump/nm) and a text editor.
instructions: Run gcc -E, -S, -c and a final link, keeping every output file.
Compare wc -l of hello.i before and after adding #include <stdio.h>.
Run objdump -d hello.o and find main's assembly.
Run nm hello.o and identify which symbol is global (T) vs undefined (U).
hints: Use gcc -v hello.c to see the sub-commands gcc actually invokes.
completion_criteria: You have hello.i, hello.s, hello.o and hello.exe
You can explain which file each flag produced and why headers bloat hello.i
